title: Rigveda 5.26: To Agni
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 5.26: To Agni: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 5.26 is a hymn of 9 verses addressed to Agni. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 5, the family book of the Atri clan. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 337r-337v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 5.26.1-2 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 1, varga 19); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 337r
translation.original_text:
1agne̍ pāvaka ro̱ciṣā̍ ma̱ndrayā̍ deva ji̱hvayā̍ | ā de̱vān va̍kṣi̱ yakṣi̍ ca ||
2taṁ tvā̍ ghṛtasnav īmahe̱ citra̍bhāno sva̱rdṛśa̍m | de̱vām̐ ā vī̱taye̍ vaha ||
translation.text:
1O AGNI, Holy and Divine, with splendour and thy pleasant tongue Bring hither and adore the Gods.
2We pray thee, thou who droppest oil, bright-rayed! who lookest on the Sun, Bring the Gods hither to the feast.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 337r (numbered 10r by the scribe) (OPenn image 337, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 5.25.6 ‹-aparājitam›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 337v (numbered 10v by the scribe), begins in RV 5.26.3 ‹vīti-hotram tvā kave dyu-mantam›. Verses 5.26.1-2 end on this page.

translation.original_ref: RV 5.26.3-9 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 1, varga 19); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 337v
translation.original_text:
3vī̱tiho̍traṁ tvā kave dyu̱manta̱ṁ sam i̍dhīmahi | agne̍ bṛ̱hanta̍m adhva̱re ||
4agne̱ viśve̍bhi̱r ā ga̍hi de̱vebhi̍r ha̱vyadā̍taye | hotā̍raṁ tvā vṛṇīmahe ||
5yaja̍mānāya sunva̱ta āgne̍ su̱vīrya̍ṁ vaha | de̱vair ā sa̍tsi ba̱rhiṣi̍ ||
6sa̱mi̱dhā̱naḥ sa̍hasraji̱d agne̱ dharmā̍ṇi puṣyasi | de̱vānā̍ṁ dū̱ta u̱kthya̍ḥ ||
7ny a1̱̍gniṁ jā̱tave̍dasaṁ hotra̱vāha̱ṁ yavi̍ṣṭhyam | dadhā̍tā de̱vam ṛ̱tvija̍m ||
8pra ya̱jña e̍tv ānu̱ṣag a̱dyā de̱vavya̍castamaḥ | stṛ̱ṇī̱ta ba̱rhir ā̱sade̍ ||
9edam ma̱ruto̍ a̱śvinā̍ mi̱traḥ sī̍dantu̱ varu̍ṇaḥ | de̱vāsa̱ḥ sarva̍yā vi̱śā ||
translation.text:
3We have enkindled thee, O Sage, bright caller of the Gods to feast. O Agni, great in Sacrifice.
4O Agni, come with all the Gods, come to our sacrificial gift: We choose thee as Invoking Priest.
5Bring, Agni, to the worshipper who pours the juice, heroic strength: Sit with the Gods upon the grass.
6Victor of thousands, Agni, thou, enkindled, cherishest the laws, Laud-worthy, envoy of the Gods.
7Set Agni Jâtavedas down, the bearer of our sacred gifts, MostYouthful, God and Minister.
8Duly proceed our sacrifice, comprising all the Gods, to-day: Strew holy grass to be their seat.
9So may the Maruts sit thereon, the Aṣvins, Mitra, Varuṇa: The Gods with all their company.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 337v (numbered 10v by the scribe) (OPenn image 338, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 5.26.3 ‹vīti-hotram tvā kave dyu-mantam›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 338r (numbered 11r by the scribe), begins in RV 5.27.2 ‹me śatā ca viṃśatim›. Verses 5.26.3-9 end on this page.
